titlePlain: Why Helm Exists: Templating a Deployment Instead of
subtitle: Lesson 21 · Deploying with Helm

steps.label: dev.yaml, staging.yaml, prod.yaml
steps.sub: 95% identical, maintained by hand in three places

steps.label: Every real change × 3
steps.sub: image tag, env var, resource limit all edited separately

steps.label: Silent drift
steps.sub: no diff, no history, no "what's actually running in prod"

code:
# deployment-dev.yaml, deployment-staging.yaml, deployment-prod.yaml
# ...nearly identical, except for a handful of lines like:

spec:
  replicas: 1          # 1 in dev, 2 in staging, 6 in prod
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: myapp:1.4.2   # tag drifts between files over time
caption: Three hand-maintained files, no shared source of truth.

eyebrow: What a Helm template looks like instead
code:
# templates/deployment.yaml
spec:
  replicas: {{ .Values.replicaCount }}
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: web
          image: "{{ .Values.image.repository }}:{{ .Values.image.tag }}"
caption: One template; {{ .Values.x }} is filled in per environment, never hand-edited.
